__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Prometheus datasource scraping the gcm-md-sequencer-aeron chart's ServiceMonitors (cluster-node, nats-bridge, line-handler-template, mock-upstream-source).

title: GCM-MD Sequencer (Aeron, phase 2)
description: Design doc §17 / implementation-steps.md Milestone 10. Covers the whole phase-2 pipeline: mock-upstream-source -> line-handler-template -> cluster-node (Aeron/Raft) -> nats-bridge -> md.sequenced -> mock-upstream-source's own verifier. Panel groupings: cluster leadership/health, end-to-end throughput, correctness invariants (should be permanently zero), backpressure/errors, replay/lag, snapshot/consensus internals.

panels.title: Leader count (must be exactly 1)
panels.description: count of cluster-node pods currently reporting sequencer_cluster_role==2 (LEADER, Aeron's Role.LEADER.code()). 0 means no leader elected; >1 would mean split-brain and should never happen.

panels.title: Per-member role (0=FOLLOWER, 1=CANDIDATE, 2=LEADER)
panels.description: sequencer_cluster_role per cluster-node pod. Watch for flapping (frequent CANDIDATE excursions) - a sign of an unstable leader, e.g. the still-open cluster-node-restart investigation (implementation-steps.md).

panels.title: Commit position
panels.description: sequencer_commit_position per member - should climb steadily and in lockstep across members in a healthy multi-member cluster.

panels.title: Pipeline throughput funnel (msg/s)
panels.description: The four stages of the phase-2 loop: mock-upstream-source publishes -> line-handler-template relays into the cluster -> nats-bridge republishes to md.sequenced -> mock-upstream-source's own consumer observes it. A sustained gap between adjacent stages points at exactly where the pipeline is bottlenecked or stalled.

panels.title: bridge_gap
panels.description: Contiguity break in sequenceIds consumed off the Aeron egress stream, before NATS. Design §9: phase-2 egress is contiguous by construction - nonzero here is an egress bug, never routine noise.

panels.title: mock_upstream_gap
panels.description: Contiguity break on the final observed egress (post-NATS), as seen by mock-upstream-source's own JetStream-backed verifier. See implementation-steps.md for the incident history behind this metric (NATS storage exhaustion, since fixed; core-NATS-drop false positives, since fixed by switching EgressConsumer to JetStream).

panels.title: mock_upstream_duplicate
panels.description: Duplicate sequenceIds seen on the final observed egress. A small, slowly-growing nonzero rate is a known, tracked artifact of JetStream's at-least-once redelivery on the verifier's own subscription (see the Nats-Msg-Id dedup-header follow-up in implementation-steps.md) rather than proof of a system-level double-publish - but a sudden jump is still worth investigating.

panels.title: sequencer_schema_mismatch
panels.description: Ingress messages that failed the configured schemaId check at the leader (design §4's REJECTED_SCHEMA verdict). Nonzero means a line handler is sending the wrong schema, or offsets are misconfigured.

panels.title: sequencer_egress_suppressed
panels.description: Messages the SuppressionGate blocked from a double-publish (design §6.4's own invariant: 'no sequenced message is ever published twice'). Expected to be nonzero occasionally around a leadership change (that's the gate doing its job); a high, steadily-climbing rate outside of failover windows would be suspicious.

panels.title: sequencer_event_tracking_evicted
panels.description: Per-source dedup/gap-tracking state evicted before being observed (a bounded-memory tradeoff in the stamping engine). Nonzero suggests the per-source tracking window is too small for the actual traffic pattern.

panels.title: bridge_checkpoint_reset
panels.description: ContiguityTracker rebasing a stale NATS-KV checkpoint after a sustained run of below-checkpoint sequenceIds - distinct from bridge_gap: this is the bridge recovering from a non-monotonic sequenceId-space reset (e.g. a single-member cluster-node losing non-persisted Archive state), not an egress bug. Should be permanently zero against a genuinely production-safe multi-member cluster (design §9); nonzero in local/dev testing is expected whenever cluster-node loses state. See ContiguityTracker's class Javadoc for the heuristic and its false-positive risk (premature rebase -> duplicate publish) if checkpoint-reset-threshold-messages is set too low for the deployment's real replay-catchup backlog.

panels.title: Per-source duplicate / gap rate
panels.description: sequencer_source_duplicate_total and sequencer_source_seq_gap_total, both tagged by source name (configured in clusterNode.sources). These are phase-1-and-phase-2-shared metric names (carried forward per design §17) - a migration-period dashboard naturally overlays both phases here.

panels.title: Publish failures / drops
panels.description: bridge_publish_failures (nats-bridge -> md.sequenced) and line_handler_publish_failures / line_handler_offer_retries (line-handler-template -> cluster). See implementation-steps.md's incident writeup for why these can spike together with NATS storage pressure.

panels.title: Silent-thread-death guards (should be permanently zero)
panels.description: bridge_loop_errors / line_handler_relay_loop_errors - count iterations where the bridge/relay poll loop caught and survived a transient exception instead of the daemon thread dying silently (a real incident this session: an uncaught NATS-storage-exhaustion exception used to kill nats-bridge's bridging thread permanently while the pod stayed Running/Ready). Nonzero means something transient is happening and being recovered from - worth alerting on even though it's not an outage by itself.

panels.title: Backpressure stall time
panels.description: *_backpressure_stall_seconds across the pipeline - time spent blocked waiting for room in a bounded publish window. Phase-1 sequencer_backpressure_stall_seconds is included for migration-period comparison.

panels.title: In-flight publish window
panels.description: *_inflight_window - current size of each bounded async-publish-ack window. Sustained pinning near its configured max (jetstream-max-in-flight) is a leading indicator of the stall/backpressure issues above.

panels.title: nats-bridge replay catch-up active
panels.description: bridge_lag_sequences: 1 while ReplayMerge is still catching up from the leader's Archive recording after downtime, 0 once merged/live. See BridgePipeline's Javadoc for why this is a coarse but real proxy, not a precise byte/sequence lag.

panels.title: Last sequenceId observed, by stage
panels.description: bridge_last_sequence_id (nats-bridge's own tail) vs line_handler_last_source_seq_num (line-handler-template's upstream tail, a different numbering space - source stream sequence, not the cluster's assigned sequenceId, but useful as a relative lag proxy for whether either side has stalled).

panels.title: sequencer_dr_replication_lag_sequences
panels.description: Registered ahead of the prod-dr work landing (Milestone 12) - stays at 0 until a real DR Archive replicator calls ClusterMetrics.setDrReplicationLagSequences(). Present now so this dashboard doesn't need a panel added later just for this.

panels.title: Snapshot duration
panels.description: sequencer_snapshot_duration_seconds (p50/p99 from the summary's sum/count) - wall-clock duration of onTakeSnapshot. A trend upward over time as the sequencer's dedup/gap-tracking state grows is worth watching.

panels.title: Raw Aeron counters (errors / flow control / back-pressure)
panels.description: aeron_counter_value{id,label} - every counter the embedded media driver exposes (design §17), one gauge per counter id/label pair (AeronCountersExporter's own Javadoc explains the snapshot-at-construction caveat). Filtered here to labels containing 'error' or 'back' as a starting point; edit the regex to explore the full set via the label filter, since Aeron's counter catalog isn't centrally documented and varies by driver version.
